name: Working for Nature / Mahi mō te Taiao grant
summary: Contestable council grants for community groups, businesses, landowners and individuals in Marlborough to restore native habitat and control pests, plus a small environmental advocacy category. Paid by reimbursement against project milestones.

amount.note: Cap for the pest-control category; habitat restoration is capped lower and advocacy lower again

eligibility.rule: Submits no more than one application per category annually
For multi-year funding, has a proven history of successful biodiversity projects
Project directly benefits Marlborough people and takes place within Marlborough
If land is not applicant-owned, has written landowner consent for ongoing support
For planting projects, uses native plants grown from suitable local seed or plant material
Does not seek staff labour, plant and equipment, monitoring cameras or non-local plants
Not work required by a resource consent, mitigation or other legal requirement
Work not done or bought before grant approval

documents: Quotes for work or goods to verify cost
Planting plan or trapline placement details
Written Council or DOC support for public land

calls.label: April application month
calls.recurring: Applications open 1 to 30 April; outcomes notified by July

status.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April.

recurring.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of their grant by July.

applicant_types.quote: One application per category is permitted annually from community organisations, businesses, landowners (including farming, forestry, winegrowing) and individuals.

geography.quote: Marlborough has been identified as one of five centres of biodiversity in New Zealand due to the concentration of endemic species

access.quote: The contestable grant scheme is administered by a sub-committee of the Environment Committee, and operates using a reimbursement model.

window.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April.

amount.quote: Protecting Marlborough: These projects control animal and plant pests that are threatening native wildlife and habitats. Grants are up to $15,000 per applicant in any one year.

effort.quote: Applications open for the month of April - from the 1 to midnight on the 30 of April.

eligibility.quote: One application per category is permitted annually from community organisations, businesses, landowners (including farming, forestry, winegrowing) and individuals.
To be eligible for this funding, the community trust or group must have a proven history of successfully undertaking environmentally beneficial biodiversity projects.
Projects must be of direct benefit to people of the Marlborough district and take place within Marlborough.
Projects undertaken on land not owned by the applicant will require written consent from the landowner, ensuring an ongoing support of the project on the land parcel into the future.
All plantings must consist of native plants grown from a suitable local sourced seed or plant material.

Personal or existing staff labour costs. Plant and equipment (e.g., chainsaws, scrub bars, etc.). Monitoring cameras and thermal monitoring devices. Exotic plants or native plants not naturally found in the Marlborough region.
Work that is required as a condition of a resource consent or mitigation, subdivision consent, entitlement application, or other legal requirement.
Work completed prior to grant approval, including past purchases.

after_award.quote: The applicant will be required to supply photos to Council immediately after planting and again 12 months later.
An accountability form will need to be completed and returned once the money is spent.

documents.quote: Quote(s) for work or goods to verify cost. Planting plan, trapline placement etc. (e.g., number and species of plants). Map showing the project area.
Letter of support by landowner (if applicable).
public land will require written support by either Council or DOC.
